utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, did you take a look at this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lucija Sebesic. I would say, based on her name and the name of her parent that this is a Croat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lucija is a Croatian name, Sebesic is also a Croatian last name?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never thought about who was Serbian and who was Croatian. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Donja Dubica, where this person was born, has a majority of Croatian inhabitants; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking only if you know.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I've finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ma'am, do you know that the Red Cross of Bosanski Samac took equal care of refugees, both of Muslim and Serbian ethnicity? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there were any Muslim refugees, and I don't know how much care they took of them. How would I know these things?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, could you please tell me the following: Did the Red Cross in Bosanski Samac distribute humanitarian aid to everybody, regardless of their ethnic origin? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you testified to the Prosecution, you mentioned that you heard from your Muslim neighbours that they received humanitarian aid: Flour, oil, and other things. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that, and I went to ask for help, and I said that the son of Cviko Bosic told me I could get that from Alija, and I never went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, are you familiar with the fact that the distribution of humanitarian aid was organised according to city quarters, city districts? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went to wherever I heard that food was being distributed, into the old hotel, Stari hotel. I don't know which neighbourhood this was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there were actually four points where this aid was being distributed?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that criteria were set up based on which humanitarian was distributed?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that since you did not register and you did not meet the criteria for receiving humanitarian aid as somebody who was receiving their pension, you were not even entitled to it?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even know registration was necessary. I have no idea. I can't say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. You mentioned in your direct examination the work obligation your brother had. You said that at the beginning he did his work obligation in his own shop, and later, if I understood you correctly, he went to another place.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He got a new boss, Milos, in his own shop. At any time of day or night, any Serb could come and say, "Chief, I need a window fixed." And my brother didn't dare ask where or when, at any time of day or night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, you have already told us this. Can I ask you just this: Was your brother, under his work assignment, in the Staklorad company, across the street from Rajco's cafe?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he did not perform his work obligation in that enterprise?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before the war he was a private entrepreneur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about 1992 and 1993, when there were no longer any materials in his own shop. Where did he perform his work obligation?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He was taken to various locations, such as Obudovac, Odzak. He was even there when the Catholic church was destroyed in Odzak. He was in the immediate vicinity of the site, in a hotel in Odzak, and that church was across the street from the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, that's a topic I'm not interested in. I only want to know, since you mentioned in your direct examination, in response to one of the questions, that two men in uniform appeared and told you they would take you to your apartment. You replied you couldn't go because you were waiting for your brother to come to lunch.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother was there when this happened. He had already come to lunch. But I said I would not go before he came to lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he came for both breakfast and lunch, if he was in Samac?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. If he was in Samac, he came in twice, for breakfast and lunch. But he never knew himself where he would be going on any particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: You mentioned that the telephones were disconnected. This will be a small digression. Was there any shelling at the time when telephones were disconnected?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was right at the beginning. I don't know if ten days after the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we talking about shelling?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no shelling at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did shelling begin?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but there was shelling. I can't remember when it began, but it was heavy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the shells came from the other side of the front line, I suppose, if you know.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say yes or no. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible -- I'm not claiming that you did any such thing, but it would have been possible to inform somebody outside on the phone of possible targets.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Telephones were disconnected only in Muslim and Croat homes, not to a single Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm perfectly sure. All the telephones of my Serb neighbours kept ringing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including your neighbour Mr. Maslic, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, if he didn't have a phone in the other place where he lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, in your testimony during direct examination, you mentioned that at the time you were rather ill and you went to the health centre of Bosanski Samac to get therapy and medication; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there for a check-up, but I didn't get a check-up or any other service. The doctor told me, "We have no medicines." Although I was pretty certain that they did have medication from donations, I couldn't get them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in any case, you went to the health centre in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the health centre of Bosanski Samac was staffed mainly by Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under work obligation, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about Mesud Nogic, who was chief of department?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, under work obligation. He wasn't chief of department; he was a slave, like everyone else, a servant.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's request. Could counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Azra Alijagic he was a doctor and a Muslim; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She married a Serb and they disappeared from Samac that same moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, the interpreters would like you to slow down when you're asking questions. And also, can the witness please pause before starting to answer so that the interpretation can be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, Ruzmir Jusufovic also worked in the health centre under work obligation?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ruzmir worked at the hospital. I don't know that he worked at the health centre, under work obligation. His wife worked at the pharmacy and he worked at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Dr. Harcinovic, a Muslim? Did he also work at the health centre of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he did before the war, and I think he was among the first who swam across the river to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Ruza Masic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brdar Ruza Masic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew her. What do you want?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she work at the health centre of Bosanski Samac under work obligation?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, for a while, but then she disappeared from Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, what was the name of the doctor who refused to give you medication or conduct the check-up?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was barely aware of my own name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the living conditions during your stay in Samac? Did you have blackouts all the time?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occasionally we had electricity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose you had problems with water as well.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means necessarily that you also had shortages of heating.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shellings were frequent, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on balance, the conditions were hard on all ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Serbs got firewood, they got wood-burning ovens, which were delivered to them from villages, and we had neither. And even if we had received firewood, I, for one, had no place to keep it, because I live on the third floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, did Serbs have electricity?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't. They had stoves and firewood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have water?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I had no water, they didn't have any either, but then we got it from the artesian wells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did shells hit all targets equally?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs were not in the streets. They were always in safe places, whereas Muslims had to go out to work, even during shelling. So it was mainly Muslims who were killed by the shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that not a single Serb was killed by a shell?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know about Savo, a mailman, who got killed sometime at the beginning. He was killed by one of the first shells and I can even tell you where exactly where he was killed. I don't know of any other Serb killed by a shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm through with this topic. You also mentioned in your testimony that throughout the time you were in Samac, page 48 or 47 of the unofficial transcript, you saw Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him. Every time I was in the street, he was there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he had a beard?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw him after the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know the date, but he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So right after the 17th of April, 1992, he was there?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I don't know the date, but he was present. He was there in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you used to see him?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the street, most often. In the marketplace I would see him walking around. I asked people what it was that he had. It's not a rifle, because a rifle is longer, and it wasn't a pistol, because a pistol is shorter, and they told me it was a Scorpion. He always had it in his right hand with a finger on the trigger. His appearance was intimidating to our people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him he had a beard?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was in uniform?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you used to see him in Dragalici during your exchange?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Dragalici. I'm not sure if he was there in Dragalici, but he was there all the time up to the moment when he said that the Croats won't have us and that we had no place to return because those pests had already occupied our homes. And that was the last time I saw him, although I believe he was present even in Dragalici, but I don't remember seeing him when we got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was in uniform with this Scorpion?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because during direct examination you said that throughout the war he wore a uniform and carried this Scorpion with his finger constantly on the trigger.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you saying?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With his finger on the trigger.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, walking in the streets of Samac, and especially in the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are sure that in those first days when you saw him, he had a beard?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention really. I still see him in my mind with this beard, with this Scorpion, and I hate to even think about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not sure that you saw Miroslav Tadic on the venue of the exchange in Dragalici?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't an exchange. I told you this already. They just took us out of the bus and moved us to another bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, ma'am. I'm asking you this: Are you certain whether you saw him in Dragalici or not?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that very place, no, but he was part of our escort, and while we had this escort, I saw him all the time walking around the bus, and I saw him before he went off to Gradiska to spend the night together with this Maslic. And I saw Maslic personally -- we must have been in Dragalici, but we --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is what I want to ask you. You were in Dragalici all the time when you came to the separation line?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but nobody would accept us, nor could they turn us back. I've already told you this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Miroslav Tadic got on the bus and told you this, was it in Dragalici, where you were standing, parked?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was some place on the highway, on the Croatian side, when he got in --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I want to know. On the highway, on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was under Serb control, Serb -- I don't know what it's called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. Was he in uniform? Was he in uniform, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miroslav Tadic, when he allegedly got on the bus to tell you this.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you even what I wore at the time. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have this Scorpion gun?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that this event you mentioned actually happened in an area protected by the UN?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw blue helmets and we were overjoyed to see them. They were on the bridge, which was closed to traffic, and in Gradiska we crossed over a pontoon bridge and we were happy that we were going to get the blue helmets protection. However, we only saw them on that bridge and never again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, ma'am: This Velja Maslic whom you mentioned, you saw him on the venue of the exchange in Dragalici?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the one who directed me. He said, "Hajra, where are you going? You should be going that way, together with the others."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know that your neighbour, Velimir Maslic, was the chairman of the Exchange Commission for the territory of Bosanski Samac? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to register and apply for exchange, you went to the Red Cross office, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you registered together with your brother?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know when my brother applied. I went there alone and I was happy to find Veljo there. He had "minister" written on his door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. About this exchange, you mentioned there were two buses: One carrying people from Samac and another carrying people from Zasavica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that 40 families of indigent population of Croat ethnicity left Zasavica at the same time as you did?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. There were only a few persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to anyone in Zasavica out of those people who left together with you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. When we moved to the Croatian bus. Pero, my son-in-law's sister, was sitting next to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you that the relatives of Mr. Pandurevic demanded that they be sent for an exchanged and moved from this area?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We didn't talk about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which Ivo Pandurevic do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivica Pandurevic from Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know one Ivo Pandurevic, an old man from Zasavica. I don't know whether he was in Samac at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see at that time a truck carrying people from Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were carrying dead bodies for exchange, and they also collected things of those people from Zasavica, and all those who turned their things over to that truck had to pay 10 Deutschmark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this truck full of things and people from Zasavica crossed over to the other side; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the dead bodies and the luggage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know, although you already mentioned this, that at this time, between the 24th and the 25th of December, 1993, a war was raging between Croats and Muslims in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there were problems about your exchange because Croats did not want to receive Muslims in exchange?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Croats told us that they hadn't even known about our group. If they had, they might have reached an agreement. Because there was nobody ready to be exchanged for us. Nobody was lined up in Croatia to cross over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, please answer with a yes or no. Do you know that there were problems involved in this exchange because there was a war between Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Christmas Eve and people didn't even know about this exchange. I strenuously insist that this was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know that several days later a large group of Serbs crossed over to the other side, from Croatia, that is, to the territory of Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, in your testimony in direct examination, when the Prosecutor asked you a question, you said that it was an open secret in Bosanski Samac that bribes were paid before an exchange.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody told me this, but only after I crossed over to the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my questions. You said it was an open secret, but you hadn't heard about it while you were in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree, then, that it was not an open secret in Bosanski Samac during your stay; it's something that you learned later.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who found out about this went there and paid, and they were happy to save their heads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's okay. You've given up. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But during your stay in Samac, you didn't know about this, you hadn't heard about this?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. But everybody who left before me did know. Everybody who got out the same way, they told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just another thing: You said in response to a question from the Prosecution that the wife of one of your nephews gave some jewellery in a box to Sveto Vasovic and that she immediately went to an exchange without being placed on any list beforehand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show this witness one document which has already been admitted in closed session. I believe it was introduced to Witness M. The number is D26/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm wondering whether it wasn't under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I would like the help of the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, it was not requested under seal for this document. It was admitted, but not under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, what is the name of this person, Fadila?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadila Drljacic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She has two children?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show this document to the witness. And perhaps we should put it on the ELMO for everyone to see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I object. Republika Srpska did not exist at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We've been through that. Just answer the questions from counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, what you see is a list of people --

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is from Serbian Republic. At that time it did not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please turn the other page. Please look at number 84. It says "Fadila Drljacic and two children." Is that the wife of your brother's son?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This clashes with your claim that she was not on the list, that she only went to be exchanged because she paid a bribe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object. That does not clash with her claim. When she made those bribes, she was not on the list. And if you look at this, I can waive for redirect examination. Her name is almost on the bottom. So when these are placed in relation to 80 names before her. It doesn't clash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's not conclusive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you said a moment ago, if I understood you correctly, that she may have been on the list, but he wouldn't let her get on the bus.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So which is true: That she wasn't on the list and she paid him a bribe, or that she was on the list?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I possibly know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I wanted to know. Let me ask you another thing. You learnt about this indirectly through your brother and your nephew?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadila herself told me about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After --?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you didn't pay anything to get on the list?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It was in their interests to clear us out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the direct examination, you mentioned another case of bribery, and you named Juro Krajinovic.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who allegedly paid 5.000 Deutschmark to Miroslav Tadic in order to get out of Bosanski Samac, and you said that Miroslav Tadic drove him and his family in his own car.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I maintain that he drove out his family. I don't know about the man himself. He was detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're sure about what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure. I was told about this. Miroslav Tadic knows that my sister's daughter is married in Zasavica and Jure and this niece's husband are close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they told you that Miroslav Tadic drove them out in exchange for 5.000 Deutschmark?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender a document. It has been disclosed to the OTP, ERN number [In English] 0005602 [Interpretation] It is a list of people who were exchanged in Dragalici on 18 September 1992. Unfortunately, I don't have an English translation. We see on this list some persons who were mentioned by the witness some time ago, and since we learned about this claim of the witness only on Thursday, we couldn't get the translation in time. So we only have the B/C/S version. And I would kindly ask for an identification number, and I would like then to show this document to the witness. I provided the interpreters with this document to facilitate their job. It's very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have a number for identification purposes only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be D49/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, did you take a look at this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read out everything that is highlighted.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "List of exchanged persons in Dragalici --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: " -- on the day of September 18, 1992. Left, under 3, Jure Krajinovic, son of Ilija, born 1995, economist. Gospava Krajinovic, called -- nicknamed Goja, with two under-aged children, the wife of Jure."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the signature, commission for the exchange of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document does not prove to me in any way that it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just tell the following to me: This family that is written down here, Jure Krajinovic and Gospava Krajinovic, are these the same people that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. These are the same people. This is the family. I would like to add the following: As far as I know, the exchanges always involved a lot of people, and I don't see why this exchange would only involve such a small number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read the letterhead up in the corner. You didn't read that.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again it says "Republika Srpska," and again I am denying this fact, because at that time Republika Srpska did not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read on. I am interested in you -- I would like you to read the following --

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exchange of persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to read it out and you can just agree that what I read out is correct. "Commission for the exchange of prisoners and arrested civilians."

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is that written?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Below Serbian municipality of Samac. And then it says "Samac, 18th of September, 1992."

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that what I just read out is written in this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but how can I know that this document is true?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, ma'am, of all the people, including your cousin, you heard that they paid 5.000 dollars -- Deutschmarks?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction, Deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Miroslav Tadic would transfer them out of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that only about Jure. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Hajrija.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Borislav Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I represent the defence of Mr. Simo Zaric. Before I ask you a number of questions, I would like to say the following on behalf of my client: He would like to express his deepest regret for everything that you and other townspeople of Samac survived in this unfortunate conflict that happened on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We needed help, and not his apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to turn your attention to some issues. Although my learned colleague asked you to wait a little bit before you start answering my question, I would like to ask you again to refrain from commenting on the events. What you have to understand is that you are a witness here and you have to testify about the facts and events. I think that in this way we can make this process that we have to undergo much easier. Ma'am, you said before this Honourable Court that you lived in the Pero Bosic Street?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pero Bosic Street number 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you live on the third or the fourth floor?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the third.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a building that also contains the Privredna Banka Sarajevo premises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Immediately next to your building there is the building called Carrington; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The movie theatre is also there?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The movie theatre was between our two buildings. We shared a joint yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my next question. So your building, the building that you lived in, and the Carrington building and the movie theatre, are around the yard and the parking lot?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what you mean by "parking lot."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The place where cars were parked.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My building and the Carrington building had a joint yard, but they had nothing to do with the movie theatre, because there was a separate wall that was separating the movie theatre from us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that the movie theatre building closed this yard from the west?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This building that you lived in, and you still live in it, from what I hear, was entered from this yard?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could enter it from the Pero Bosic Street. You entered my entrance from that street. I lived in the first entrance. Those that lived in the second entrance would enter their building from the yard, but I was entering the street from -- directly from the street direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In this same building, Safet Hadzialijagic, called Policeman, also resided; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the other part of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are familiar with the fact that Safet Hadzialijagic, called Coner was the head of the water supply system in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have just one clarification. In the transcript, page 64, line 8, it says "policeman." It is not a policeman. It is Coner. It's a nickname and has nothing to do with police. It doesn't mean in our language policeman or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So instead of the word "policeman," it should just be Coner. That's the nickname. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Safet Hadzialijagic, called Coner, is a Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mihajlo Topolovac, nicknamed Mile?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will remind you. He is a retired police commander in Samac.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the same street and the same house where Safet Hadzialijagic used to live.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, up until the war, I didn't even know who lived in my entrance. I don't know. Maybe if I saw him, I would recognise him. Just like you. Well, I did actually know your name as well, but this Topolovac as well, I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know Mr. Vaso Antic? He was a journalist and the director of Radio Samac.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Radio Samac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both the Serbian and the one before the 17th.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I met him during the war. I hadn't known him before. I also met his wife then. I knew where she worked. I knew her by sight, but I didn't know her name. He lived in the other part of my building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that in this same entrance, Mladen Djordjic also resided, the son of Rada and Andjelko?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that in this same street, Pero Bosic Street, the house of Bicic Muhamed and Bicic Hasan was also located?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second house from my apartment was theirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. Would you agree that this distance was maybe about 40 metres?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe even less, from my entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In this same street, they also had their pizzeria, called Rendezvous?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It was immediately next to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to that. Let's slow down. Would you agree that maybe about 80 metres from your entrance there was the house of Sabrija Dagovic and his sons, Safet and Esad Dagovic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where their house was. I don't know how many metres this is, but I can tell you how many houses it was from my entrance to their house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified here that on the 17th of April you saw an explosion in the pizzeria called Rendezvous in Pero Bosic Street.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard an explosion nearby, and I ran towards the window, because there was a lot of shooting that previous night, so I went to the window to see what was going on. And a hand-held rocket launcher was thrown into this pizzeria, and this was on the 18th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any street lighting at that moment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for it. It had already dawned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to correct this. We noticed an error in the transcript. If I understood you correctly, it said this happened on the 18th. You said this happened on the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early morning hours, just after it had dawned. While there was shooting, there was some attack going on, but I have no idea who was attacking and who was defending. And I also -- the primary school was also burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's slow down.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please let me finish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just focus on the pizzeria Rendezvous and the events that happened in the Djuro Djakovica and Pero Bosic streets. That's what we're interested in right now. You said that you saw some soldiers at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them when I saw this explosion. I took a look and I saw smoke rising out of the pizzeria. Below my window there were soldiers, and I thought these were Croatian soldiers, because I had just come back from Croatia and I thought that they were the only ones that had camouflage uniforms. I thought this was a Croatian army. This is why I ran to Veljko to ask Veljko and to ask Milan Babic to ask what the Croatian army was doing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had already mentioned this. So these soldiers that you saw and who fired the hand-held rocket launcher towards the pizzeria, those were the ones that were in your street

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These soldiers were below my window, in my street. I don't know who was by the pizzeria, but I'm assuming that probably it was the same people who were attacking at that time. As far as I know, there were no other armed men other than this military that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's slow down. You had said earlier that somebody was shooting from a hand-held rocket launcher towards the pizzeria Rendezvous. I would like to ask you the following: Do you know what a hand-held rocket launcher is?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When we were talking, they all said that it was a Zolja, but I don't really know what that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would agree that you don't know what a Zolja is?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you didn't see this precise moment when something or someone shot or threw some explosive object into the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I heard the explosion, that was -- after that I ran to the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we've cleared this up. Thank you very much. So these soldiers that were below your window, whom you could see, were dressed in --?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms. So if I understood you correctly, these uniforms looked very much like uniforms worn by Croatian soldiers, who you saw while you were in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought only Croatian soldiers had these uniforms. I didn't know that there were other armies too that had them. I only thought that Croatians had them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's slow down. Thank you. On this 17th of April, 1992, did you see, on the Pero Bosic and parts of the Djuro Djakovica Street, movements of groups of armed civilians?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I didn't look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't explain anything. Just say if you saw it or not.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day, the 17th of April, 1992, in the yard of your building and the Carrington building, did you see any armed persons that were wearing civilian clothes predominantly?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see anybody wearing civilian clothes who was armed. I only saw these --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're done with that. We're finished. Thank you. On that day, did you see any kind of gathering of people at all in the yard of your building and the Carrington building?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My window was facing the street. It didn't look into the window -- into the yard. I was scared of these soldiers that entered my entrance. I only looked through the window, or at times I would only just sit in the armchair. I had no intention whatsoever to remember or to pay attention to these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you then agree that on that day, the 17th of April, 1994 [As interpreted], during that whole day, you did not observe what was going on in the street or in the yard of your building?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I observed what was going on in the street from time to time, but it never occurred to me to see what was going on in the yard, because that would have meant that I had to go out into the hall and then go to another window. So that never happened. But I did watch what was going on in the Pero Bosic Street, and also the part -- a part of the Djuro Djakovica Street that I could see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Page 69, line 8, it says 17th of April, 1994. That should be corrected for the record. She was exchanged and deported in 1993. It should be at least corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think counsel can see the date and he'll correct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these events took place on the 17th of April, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ma'am, do you know Ibela Ibrahim Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell this Chamber: On that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, can we have -- is it the correct name?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction. It's Ibrahim Salkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought that's what counsel had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is an error. The name is wrong. I'm going to read it out again. I asked about Ibrahim Salkic, called Ibela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Ibrahim Salkic, called Ibela?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that -- I'm not aware that his name is Ibrahim, but I know Ibela Salkic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just know his nickname, as is our custom, but we are talking about the same person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I don't know if his name is Ibrahim, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, in these moments when you were watching the Pero Bosic Street, did you see Mr. Salkic go along the Pero Bosic Street together with a group of armed civilians?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Salkic go along the street, and he had his arms raised, and he was saying, "I'm handing over my gun and nothing -- surrender your weapons," but I didn't see anything else. He was also saying, "Nothing will happen to anybody." He had come from Djuro Djakovica Street from the health centre direction, and he then turned into the Pero Bosic Street towards the department store.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to ask for some clarification of the transcript and of interpretation, because here it says: "And he had his arms raised." It's page 70, line 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since it can be interpreted as arms as arms or -- actually, I believe that accurate translation should be his weapon, because that's what -- that's what we heard from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps counsel can go over that so that we get the correct evidence from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was the following: When you saw Ibela, Ibrahim Salkic, how did you see him? If I understood you correctly, you said that his hands and arms were raised, that he had a rifle in his hand, and he was calling people to surrender their weapons and nothing would happen to them if they did so.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but I don't know what kind of a weapon he had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a rifle or something?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that. That was the only rifle that I saw on a civilian, if that was a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Drljacic, could you please tell us what day it was when you saw Mr. Salkic in this pose with his arms raised and with this rifle in his hand.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was on the same day, the 17th, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, is this a good moment to make -- start our break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- yes, but before we go, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Just a brief question for arranging the remainder of this afternoon. Could counsel give us an idea how much longer they will be with this witness? I ask that because the next witness is in his hotel room and if there's no chance of reaching him today, I'd like to be able to release him so he doesn't have to be stuck in his hotel room waiting for a telephone call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. How many more minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I will be done in about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, are you going to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, no question on behalf of Mr. Blagoje Simic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you can estimate that. In the meantime, we shall have our break and continue at 1805 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you allow me, Your Honours just for the record, the Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic doesn't wish to cross-examine this witness, according to the instruction of the defendant, Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. Will you please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Drljacic, you said a moment ago that it seems to you it was the same day when you saw Ibrahim Salkic. Do you allow for the possibility that you saw Ibrahim Salkic on the 18th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could easily be true, because, as I said, I was in a state of shock. But in any case, it was in the afternoon, not in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that on the same day, some armed people entered your entranceway. Do you allow for the possibility that these men too came on the 18th of April?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 17th, in the morning. That was just after my sighting of the troops downstairs. Because I walked to Veljo's apartment to ask him how come they were there. And then I went to Uncle Juro's because neither Milan nor Veljo were at home, so I went downstairs to see Uncle Juro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, we've already heard that. Do you know that Ibrahim Salkic was a member of the SDA? Say that you don't know if you don't know.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move to a different topic now, namely, you stated before this Trial Chamber that you knew Mr. Simo Zaric well.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Simo Zaric's wife is Muslim?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that she is a Muslim, don't you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that Mr. Zaric and his wife have a son named Mirela?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mrs. Koviljka Omeralagic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. It's his sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean Simo Zaric's sister?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is her husband a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you aware of the fact that Simo's sister, Jelena, is also married to a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know Simo's sister, Dr. Nada, who is married to a Croat?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I only know Koviljka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, by any chance, that Mr. Zaric's kum is Kasim Hasumovic, a Muslim from his Bosanski Samac, the witness at his wedding?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know the man?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was my neighbour in my childhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can confirm that he is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that Simo Zaric has a daughter, Natasa, who is married to a Croat?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we agree that you don't know Mr. Simo Zaric very well?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him from the time when he lived in Samac. He was a boy when he came to Samac. I was not interested in his roots, as he was probably not interested in mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. Mr. Hasumovic was the best man at Simo Zaric's wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move to a different topic now. You said that you listened to Mr. Zaric speak on the Serbian Radio Samac all the time.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that on those occasions he said bad, derogatory things about --

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take it easy. -- members of the Muslim ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a radio receiver in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every has one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a TV set?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Can you, with any degree of certainty, tell us when was the first time that you heard on Serbian Radio Samac or on TV any address or statement by Mr. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the date, but I did hear him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see him on TV? Did you see Mr. Simo Zaric in some sort of special programme?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He made an appearance, but I don't know what programme it was. I already told you, I was in a deep state of shock. It was a surprise to me, especially seeing him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. I quite understand, Mrs. Drljacic. But you are testifying to some very serious things, and we must all do our best to establish the truth. So if you can remember, we'll appreciate it, but nobody will put any pressure on you. After all the time that has passed since, could you agree with this piece of information: You saw Mr. Zaric on television on the 30th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what date it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that this programme included interviews of Mr. Tihic? He was interviewed by a journalist from Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember watching Tihic, Hadzialijagic, and who was the third man?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you perhaps remember that it was Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that he was interviewed on that programme by journalist from Novi Sad, as well as Mr. Omer Nalic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was it Novi Sad or Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm telling you now that it was Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have that interview given by Mr. Simo Zaric to that journalist of the Novi Sad radio and television, and the Trial Chamber is in possession of that interview. And after your statement to the effect that Mr. Simo Zaric spoke about Muslims in a very insulting way, I re-read that interview for the umpteenth time, and I did not find any derogatory reference at all to the Muslim or the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that I heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, before the witness answer. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object. The issue isn't whether Mr. Pisarevic finds something derogatory; it's up to the witness. It's the witnesses' memory, it's the witness's thoughts that are important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And this is with regard to the TV show, not the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not watch Zaric on TV. I listened to him speak on radio Serbian Samac. It grated on my ears to hear Serbian Samac for the first time. I couldn't understand why it should be Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that. As for the objection of Mr. Weiner, I wasn't recollecting anything. I only looked up what Mr. Zaric actually said, and that is relevant because we have information that it was precisely that interview which was broadcast on Radio Samac several times, and it is quite possible that the witness heard this very interview on Radio Serbian Samac.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which interview it was, but I heard him speak. I heard him say very bad things about Muslims on Radio Serbian Samac. I can't say about the TV, because I didn't watch him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Drljacic, you confirmed a moment ago, and very convincingly so, that you watched this special programme, because you watched and listened to all the participants in that special programme.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I listened to them all. I saw all those people, but I had no strength to listen to all of what was said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What you heard on Radio Samac, were those live programmes? Did Mr. Zaric talk to a journalist an announcer? Because from what you are saying, I'm getting the impression that he was the announcer himself on Radio Serbian Samac.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say whether it was an interview. I don't know. Maybe I didn't listen to the entirety of the programme, but I know that I heard him one day and then again three or four days later. It was horrible to my mind that he was saying those things, he in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, try to remember. Did anyone who edited the broadcasts of Serbian Radio Samac announce that Mr. Simo Zaric would be speaking?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said I may not have heard the entirety of the programme. I just remember what was painful for me to hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. If I understood you correctly, you only conclude that Mr. Zaric spoke because you believe you recognised his voice.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, because other people too said, "Did you hear what Simo said?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your claim is based on your ability to tell the voice of Mr. Simo Zaric, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's not what she said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: She just said, "Absolutely. When he asked about, "and because other people too said, 'Did you hear what Simo said?'"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll ask the following question of Mrs. Drljacic. On what basis do you claim before this Trial Chamber that you listened to Mr. Zaric speak on Serbian Radio Samac?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please don't try to make a fool out of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not my intention.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simo Zaric knows me as well as I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not in dispute. Please tell me: Was he announced by the announcer or did you just hear his voice? That's all I'm asking. Please tell the Court so that the Trial Chamber can hear on what basis you reached that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain that it was he who spoke, and I recognised his voice. Please let me finish. Very often, people told each other: "Did you hear what Simo said?" And I know what I heard. It was Simo Zaric. No mistake about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you again. This claim of yours is based on your ability to distinguish the voice of Mr. Simo Zaric, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not the only witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are the only one I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the other witnesses testified to this too, and I couldn't have made this up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. On the 30th of April, 1998, you gave a statement to the investigators of the Tribunal in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1998. At least that's what it says on your statement. It's here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is one of those situations where we have an interview. It is not signed, it's never been reviewed. It's an interview. We're not talking about an in-depth statement. This is one of those handful of witnesses where we've had that problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You are saying this the statement wasn't signed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It was not signed. It says at the end, "This statement was not re-read to the witness and therefore the witness has not had the opportunity to verify or acknowledge the accuracy or truth of the statement."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So it's not a statement. There was an interview of some kind. Whether it was with several people, one person, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem, Your Honours. Mr. Weiner is right in saying that this is an unsigned statement and was not read to the witness. So I'll rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Drljacic, you had an interview with the investigators of The Hague Tribunal and you provided them with certain information about what you had seen; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I confirmed this during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember that in this interview you never spoke about listening to Mr. Simo Zaric on the radio or seeing him on television?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I did not mention it. Perhaps I didn't remember to. But in the meantime, I met a lot of people, and maybe I remembered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remember or did somebody remind you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remembered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you remembered it. In that interview you made only one reference to Mr. Simo Zaric and Mr. Miroslav Tadic saying that you knew them before the war and that you thought they were some sort of commanders in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about the 4th Detachment. I was in Samac. I don't know anything about that and please don't ask me any more questions about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not. I'm just telling you what you said in the interview from 1998. When that interview was conducted, did you know that Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic had surrendered voluntarily to the Tribunal in The Hague, together with Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave that interview much earlier. And allow me to say this: I knew from the press - I was reading Belgrade and Bosnians newspapers at the time - that he said, when he was seen off, "I'm going there to tell the truth, and if I had to do it again, I would do it."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember it very well. Thank you. You don't know this, but I'll tell you that Mr. Simo Zaric surrendered himself voluntarily to the Tribunal in The Hague on the 24th of February, 1998. Do you agree with me that if you gave your interview on the 30th of April, then you must have given it later.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... they're both speaking at the same time. I'm sorry. I missed part of the question and part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can see the question on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine. They're starting to speak over each other and we're not getting things at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection withdrawn. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the counsel can ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that you had this interview with the investigators of The Hague Tribunal after the surrender of Mr. Simo Zaric to The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I gave some additional statements, but the interview was given before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not my intention, Mrs. Drljacic, to show you this interview, but I can read here: "Unofficial interview with Hajrija Drljacic 30th April 1998 attended by Agnes Inderhaug, investigator, and Diana Barbaric interpreter.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. Excuse me. I talked to Mr. Roy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when was that? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does the date matter?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, everything matters to us. This business is too important for any unclarities. Did Mr. Roy re-read the statement to you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but if I signed it, then my signature is still there, and I'm not avoiding anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it before the interview with Mrs. Agnes Inderhaug or before?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I can't place that name at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Agnes Inderhaug. It's a Mrs. or a Miss, who works as an investigator in The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the first time I talked to a lady whose name I don't remember at all. It was in 1997, maybe even end of 1996. The first time that I ever learned of the existence of this wonderful court, for which I am so grateful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this information to the effect that you had interviews with other investigators. We did not have that information, and we'll pursue it and see what we're going to do about it. You also made a claim here about Mr. Simo Zaric. Were you ever in Odzak before the 31st of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during the war. How was I supposed to get out?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. My brother went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw Mr. Simo Zaric in Odzak, did you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went to Odzak during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell the Trial Chamber now: On what basis do you claim that Simo Zaric was a commander in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
