utterances.text: He held some superior executive post. I don't know which. But Simo Zaric knows about it very well. The day the church was destroyed in Odzak, my brother, Teufik, was in a hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, how do you know Mr. Simo Zaric knows this? Please don't do this sort of thing. I'm just asking you: How do you know he was a commander? We are not disputing that he was in Odzak, but you are telling us that he was a commander. We need to clarify this. Was he a commander? How do you know that? If you don't know that, please tell us so.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of our people who had to go and do forced labour came back and said, "Simo Zaric is some sort of big cheese over there."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard it from others.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from one or two people, but from many people, all of those who went to forced labour in Odzak, and Mr. Simo Zaric knows how many there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many people there were on work obligation in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the number, but I can enumerate my relatives who worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, your 20 minutes is over. Remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was just done. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just -- if he has a few more questions, I have no objection to him questioning more. I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He said he's finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic -- yes, he said he's finished. Go ahead, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Drljacic, I have some questions for you based on some of the questions that you were asked. You were shown a document. The first document you were shown, D42/3 - there's no need to show it to her - there was a name on that document, Bahra Drljacic. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bahra.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bahra. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She is my sister. She is married to somebody in Serbia and she lives there. She is currently in Paris, but she is a citizen of Serbia. She was not in Samac, even though she was in the list as if she was using the services of the Red Cross, but that was not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said she was not. It indicates she was receiving Red Cross assistance. Was she in Bosanski Samac in the spring or summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no way. Her husband was very sick at the time, and there was no way that she could have been in Samac. I don't know really how she could have gotten in or left the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is she the person who you communicated by telephone to in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Is there a volume problem or -- could the translator say something?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: One, two, three, testing. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Try it again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: One, two, three, testing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, what number on the list was that name?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I believe it was 247. Yes, number 247, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your phone went out, was she the person who had a Serb friend whose telephone was working that you would call -- who you would call in Serbia? Is that that same sister?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The eldest sister died, and she is the only sister that I have left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there was some talk about registration. There was a document showing certain people who were receiving food from the Red Cross. Did anyone ever tell you that you had to register in order to receive food?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever told me this. I asked why this notice wasn't posted just like the other ones in which we were order that had we had to wear white armbands, or other ones, but I really don't like to remember this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just take a few questions and I'll get off this subject. Do you -- any of the people who you spoke to who received milk or bread, did they tell you that they went down and registered first?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this list my oldest sister is also listed. She died later. And even she didn't tell me that I had to register somewhere, nor was she able to register herself. I don't even know whether she received this humanitarian aid or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, your sister, or your brother have used milk or bread during the spring and summer of 1992? Could you have used that milk or bread from the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning, we had -- all of us did have help, but that time didn't last long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the summer and the spring of 1992, could you have used that help from the Red Cross, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, that happened in April, maybe one part of May as well, in 1992. We received this help in the yard of the local commune in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But ma'am, after April, could you have continued to use that help?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said this. While the food was being distributed there, in this location, I was getting it along with everybody else, but later you know what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move to one of the other documents that you were shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we please see document D26/3, and place ter -- either -- both ter and -- both English and the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, could you look at the second page of that list. I invite your attention to number 84.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Almost at the bottom, is that your niece, Fadila, Avdo's husband?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any date of birth next to her name?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is an error here. She had two children, and here it says that she only had one. Oh, I apologise. That is the line below. I apologise. Yes, it says "two children." I didn't look at the right line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there are only four names after her on that list of 88; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, I want you to look at one more thing. Look at both pages. Is there a number next to every name on those two pages?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number by every name, as an ordinal number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A number to the left of every name. There are numbers 1 through 88.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you now show her D49/3 ter, ID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at it for a moment and we'll put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are there any people on that list -- we just saw a list with 88 names. Every single one had a number next to it. Are there any people on that list that have no number next to them?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are numbers by every name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the last name, Krajinovic Gospava?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is no number here because she was added later. She was added later. She does not have a number by her name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified in this Court that Juro Krajinovic paid to have his family taken out of Bosanski Samac. Those people at the bottom of the list that don't have a number, do they constitute the family of Juro Krajinovic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mrs. Gospava is his wife, and two under-age children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it doesn't say how they were brought to the exchange. Does it say whether they came in a vehicle or whether they went by bus? Is there any indication there?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few questions concerning the radio and television. In your previous interview there was no discussion about radio or television. During that interview -- first tell me: How long did that interview last, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me. I am not objecting to this, but it wasn't quite clear to me what was the question, because we just heard that there were at least two interviews with this witness. So if my colleague can clarify: Was it the interview with investigator called Yves Roy, or maybe the other interview, or one of these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. He should be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. I was going to say that she said she spoke to Yves Roy. They didn't press that issue and ask: Was it an interview? Did you sign something? Was there paper? Did he take notes? There was no discussion as to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long did that last? With regard to the interview with Agnes Inderhaug on 30th April 1998, did -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, my learned friend, but something is confusing me. This is page 89, line 17. The question was: "A few questions concerning the radio and television," and now we are jumping into another topic with the Yves Roy interview. So I would really appreciate it if he can clarify this part of transcript for the sake of the proceedings, because otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that you get to understand which interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which interview. We have radio, television, now Yves Roy, Agnes Inderhaug. It's a lot of interviews. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weiner will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour -- all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, we're talking about not the interviews you heard on the radio. We're talking about the interviews that you had with the personnel from the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you recall the interview you had with Ms. Inderhaug back in April of 1998? Do you remember speaking with her?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean directly, in person, or over the phone?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Why don't you tell me: When you spoke with Ms. Inderhaug in this informal interview, was it over the telephone or was it in person, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I really don't remember the lady's name. I just simply didn't keep it in my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. No problem. But when you spoke with that lady, did you speak to her in person? Was she sitting with you? Or did you speak to her over a telephone?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I talked both on the phone as well. I didn't talk to a woman in person in Salt Lake City at all. I only talked to Mr. Roy. That's how I pronounced his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you spoke with a woman, you spoke over the telephone?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to a woman on the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in that interview, or it's -- in that informal interview over the telephone, there is no discussion concerning Simo Zaric making derogatory statements on the radio. Did she ever ask you during that informal interview on the telephone any specific questions relating to radio or television broadcasts?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not remember. I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there was mention by counsel of Mr. Zaric having certain relatives that were either Muslim or Croatian. He had these relatives through marriage. Let's go after the war starts. After the war starts, did you ever hear Simo Zaric say anything complimentary about Muslims over the radio?

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. He immediately transferred his family to Serbia, and he was with the brother of his wife. His brother's wife [as interpreted] was almost like his personal escort. They were always together. And there is another thing that I haven't mentioned before. When Mr. Zaric was in Odzak, he would very often come to my building in the evening with the wife's brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you never heard him say anything complimentary about Muslims. What about Croats? Did you ever hear Simo Zaric say anything complimentary about Croatians on the radio? And this is after the war began.

utterances.speaker: HAJRIJA DRLJACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Drljacic, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. You are now free. You can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution? Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we start with another witness, is it maybe the right moment that we tender some translations that we have received recently?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Because we have just five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We may as well have documents available. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: May I ask the witness who has been waiting out there that -- sorry. May I tell the witness who has been waiting out there that he's free to go back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can start him in the morning. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'm grateful to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Meaning the afternoon tomorrow, 1415. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have received the official translation of the document D20/4. It was a receipt confirming that the witness - his name is protected - has received certain weapons. And I already gave this translation to our colleagues from the Prosecution, so I don't believe that there will be any problems in this respect. D20/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Are we waiting for the usher to assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have a copy for the Trial Chamber and the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There are two more documents, if Your Honour remembers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can discuss them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While witness Esad Dagovic was testifying here for the first time, we took certain photographs of Mr. Zaric's handbag. It was made by -- with assistance of the Registry, and now we do have photographs of Mr. Zaric's bag. I was instructed by the Trial Chamber that as soon as we receive it, I should tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I have actually two different photographs. One is front side, and the backside of Mr. Zaric's bag. So I would ask for a number for this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution have copies already?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. There's no objection from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I may have the number for the evidence of these two from the Registry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The problem is they haven't -- didn't hand it in because when she issues a number, she has to immediately record that. You can go on with the third document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These are two documents, two photographs and the third is translation. And that's all. Well, with permission, maybe I could just approach the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Since we don't know what is happening to the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I confirm that D20/4 ter ID is now D20/4 ter, and the English translation, D20/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The two photographs showing the handbag, the front of the photograph will be D24/4, and the back of the handbag will be D25/4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until tomorrow afternoon at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
